jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Pacing
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Pacing is Anthropic's work to make sure that, as AI capabilities advance, enough time and effort goes into making them safe. It covers the safety commitments we make and carry out ourselves, the public policy we develop and support, and the research and communication that help people understand how quickly AI is progressing and what that could mean. We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to run Pacing. It spans many projects led by people across Safety, Research, Policy, Legal, Communications, and Engineering, most of whom have other responsibilities too. You'll make sure each project has an owner, a clear outcome, and a date, and that leaders have high visibility and can make tradeoff decisions. You'll work closely with the team responsible for our Responsible Scaling Policy and support every project lead in delivering on their commitments. The questions and strategies relevant to this program will change rapidly as the frontier evolves. You'll need enough technical depth to drive discussions about model training, evaluations, and compute, and the judgment to identify which decisions belong with cross-functional partners and which you can make yourself. We're looking for a generalist who can ship quickly and iteratively and drive accountability towards high-level, ambiguous objectives. Key responsibilities Own the Pacing program end to end, keeping one accurate view of projects, owners, milestones, dependencies, and gaps that drives action from leadership and project leads Turn strategy from executive sponsors into scoped projects with measurable outcomes and timelines for execution, and drive concrete proposals to decisions Run the operating rhythm, including working sessions with project leads, regular written updates, and effective executive reviews, and follow decisions and action items through to completion Work with the Responsible Scaling Policy team and researchers to define the evidence and sign-off a model needs at key points in training and deployment, and make those reviews a dependable part of how we work Track the public and internal commitments Anthropic makes on pacing, and sequence the work, publications, and events behind them with Policy and Communications Partner with Legal throughout the lifespan of each project, and operate with high integrity on confidential and sensitive work Define how progress is measured, report against it candidly, and recommend which projects and practices to continue, change, or stop Use Claude to build automations to allow teams to have broader and deeper impact Minimum qualifications Experience leading multiple complex technical programs that span organizations and involve engineering or research teams, from ambiguous goals through delivery Strong program management skills, including program planning, milestone and dependency tracking, and risk management across many concurrent projects Technical fluency sufficient to identify risks and challenge tradeoffs in how frontier AI models are trained, evaluated, and deployed Working knowledge of AI safety and the main debates about how frontier AI should be developed and governed A track record of delivering through senior leaders and teams who don't report to you, including when it meant changing how they work Experience preparing decisions for executives, including framing options, making a recommendation, and recording the outcome Sound judgment and discretion with confidential and sensitive information Preferred qualifications Experience at a frontier AI developer, a government AI institute, an independent evaluator, or an AI safety or governance research organization Hands-on experience with frontier AI safety work, such as safety frameworks, safety cases, risk reports, model evaluations, or reviews of model training or deployment Familiarity with how AI progress is measured, including compute, capability trends, and the use of AI to speed up AI research Experience delivering programs that combine technical work with public policy, or that bring together experts from different organizations Experience managing published commitments or high-visibility public releases Experience building a program from zero and reshaping it as the strategy evolved The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $290,000 — $365,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you! About the Role The Simulation team builds software, models, and environments to test on-road autonomous robot behavior and evaluate autonomy changes before deployment. We are hiring an Autonomy Simulation Engineer to improve simulation fidelity and accelerate the development and validation of autonomous delivery robots. You will develop production simulation software and models of robot behavior and interactions with the environment, using real-world data and repeatable experiments to calibrate and validate them. Working closely with autonomy and robotics engineers, you will own projects from design through validation and report to the Simulation Lead. We expect this role to be hybrid, with some time in-office and some time remote. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Develop and maintain the simulation engine and supporting software. Build and improve simulation models of robot behavior, other participants, and their interactions. Calibrate and validate simulation models against real-world behavior using controlled, repeatable experiments. jobs.title: Clinical Study Monitor
jobs.description: Position Summary: The Clinical Study Monitor oversees the day-to-day execution and monitoring of clinical studies involving in vitro diagnostic (IVD) devices, focusing on companion diagnostics (CDx) developed with pharmaceutical and academic partners. You will ensure studies meet protocol, company SOPs, and regulatory requirements (ICH-GCP, FDA, IVDR) while prioritizing data quality, subject safety, and inspection readiness. At Natera, we remember there is a person behind every sample . We operate with urgency and scientific rigor to get meaningful products into the hands of clinicians and patients . This role works closely with Clinical Affairs leadership and cross-functional teams to drive study site compliance. You need a deep understanding of diagnostic lab operations and CDx studies, and the urgency to drive quality data without waiting for perfect structure. Primary Responsibilities: Serve as the primary point of contact for testing sites, ensuring protocol compliance, subject safety, and data quality align with GCP, FDA, and IVDR requirements. Execute monitoring activities based on the study-specific plan, including source data verification (SDV), essential document review, specimen tracking, and resolving sample handling issues. Drive the operational execution of clinical studies, from start-up and site qualification through routine monitoring and close-out. Prepare clear, objective monitoring visit reports, tracking site findings, protocol deviations, and CAPAs through to resolution. Take ownership of developing study-related documents, relying on strong judgment to move work forward even when standard processes are still being built. Collaborate across Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, and Quality Assurance to align on study execution and quality expectations. Support IRB/EC submission activities and ensure ongoing ethical compliance. Manage study documentation, including preparation, review, filing, and archiving in the Trial Master File (TMF). Support audit readiness by preparing monitoring summaries and participating in internal audits or regulatory inspections. Identify, escalate, and resolve study risks, protocol deviations, and reportable events (e.g., adverse events) in accordance with regulations. Step in and solve problems outside your immediate scope when the team or the study needs it. Work regularly with PHI, maintaining current status on all HIPAA, Human Subjects Protection, and GCP training requirements. Qualifications: BA/BS degree in life sciences, nursing, or a related field (advanced degree such as MS or MPH is a plus). Minimum of 4 years of clinical research experience, including at least 2 years monitoring IVD and/or CDx studies. Strong knowledge of GCP, ISO 20916, IVDR, and/or FDA regulations (21 CFR Part 812) relevant to diagnostic studies. Working knowledge of diagnostic laboratory operations. Ability to travel up to 40% for site visits, audits, and investigator meetings. Must pass a post-offer criminal background check. Nice to Have: Experience in oncology, molecular diagnostics, or precision medicine. Experience supporting CDx studies, including pharmaceutical co-development or bridging studies. Familiarity with electronic data capture (EDC) systems, CTMS, sample tracking platforms, and electronic records requirements (21 CFR Part 11). Certification in clinical research (e.g., ACRP-CP, CCRA, CCRP). Prior experience in a regulated diagnostic or medical device environment. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Strong project management skills with the ability to coordinate and execute multiple studies. Clear, direct communication that builds trust and alignment with clinicians, partners, and internal teams. High attention to detail and a problem-solving mindset to proactively mitigate study risks. Ability to interpret complex clinical protocols, regulatory guidance, and laboratory procedures. Capable of writing clear, defensible monitoring findings and reports. Able to adapt quickly and maintain rigorous quality standards in a fast-moving, mission-driven environment where patient outcomes are the priority. Familiarity with biosample management and biobanking best practices. Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Physical Demands & Work Environment: Duties are performed in a hybrid or office setting requiring computer use, video conferencing, and occasional work during non-standard hours to meet deadlines or coordinate with external partners. The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Remote USA $108,200 — $140,000 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic gives independent external evaluators access to our models, our people, and our safety practices so that they can assess risks, processes, and policies. We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to establish and deepen our partnerships with these external reviewers and embedded evaluators to support a thriving frontier evaluation ecosystem. You'll be the main point of contact for our existing partners, deepening our support so that they can work effectively and produce high-quality, rigorous, independent publications. You'll separately broaden the portfolio of organizations we are working with, managing the funnel from first conversation through contracting, onboarding, and day-to-day access, culminating in published reports. You'll evolve our current time-intensive manual processes into a system that can support many evaluators at once, working with teams across Safety, Research, Security, Legal, People Services, IT, Policy, and Communications. Within six months, you should be able to take a new evaluator from contract negotiation to first published report with minimal involvement from senior leaders. You'll need the technical depth to work out with researchers and engineers what access, tooling, and evidence an evaluation requires, and the judgment to resolve most questions quickly and escalate the few that need it, while balancing evaluators' need for access with Anthropic's requirements to protect its customers, its security, and its confidential information. We're looking for a generalist who can ship quickly and iteratively, and who earns trust on both sides. Key responsibilities Own the external evaluator program end to end, including our relationships with evaluator organizations and the pipeline of future partners Take each evaluator from first conversation through scoping, contracting, onboarding, access, and review to a published report Define the stages and tiers of working with evaluators, and develop information access policies that meet evaluators' needs while protecting security and confidential information Drive evaluators' access and information requests to fast, well-documented decisions in partnership with Research, Security, Legal, and IT Drive the technical design of evaluator access with Security, IT, and infrastructure teams, including permissions, environments, and monitoring, and close gaps between policy and technical controls without slowing evaluators down Run the review process for evaluator reports against agreed timelines and redaction criteria, while protecting evaluators' ability to publish their own conclusions Scope evaluations with researchers and engineers, turning evaluators' questions about training, monitoring, and alignment into concrete requirements for model access, data, tooling, and compute, and planning capacity for each new evaluator Turn evaluators' technical findings into research and engineering work with owners and dates, and drive accountability for how Anthropic responds Keep the company informed with regular updates on how the program is going, and clear guidance on how to work with evaluators Collect feedback from evaluators and internal teams, run retrospectives, and iterate on policies and practices Use Claude and work with engineering teams to build the tooling the program runs on, such as access provisioning, request tracking, and report review Support a thriving ecosystem of evaluators by sharing what we learn about running independent evaluation well Minimum qualifications Experience leading complex technical programs with engineering or research teams, from ambiguous goals through delivery Experience managing relationships with external organizations, including scoping work, navigating contracting, setting expectations, and resolving disagreements Strong program management skills, including program planning, milestone and dependency tracking, and risk management across many concurrent workstreams Technical fluency in how frontier AI models are trained, evaluated, and monitored, sufficient to define technical requirements, identify technical risks, and challenge tradeoffs with researchers and engineers Sound judgment and discretion with confidential and sensitive information The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $290,000 — $365,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. jobs.description: Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com . Location: Reddit has a flexible-first workforce. Don't live near our New York office? No worries: you can work remotely from anywhere on the US East Coast (Eastern Time). The Ads Foundational Representations (AFR) team develops signals and representations of Reddit’s core entities (ads, posts, users, and so on), capturing the semantic, contextual, and behavioral information that Reddit Ads needs. We work on building embeddings to understand content and users' interests based on the content they engage with. Our team has the potential to highlight one of Reddit's biggest differentiators: genuinely curated, high-quality, extremely relevant, and daily updated organic content. We are a Machine Learning/Data heavy team with a focus on the following areas: Multimodal & Content Embeddings - Make sense of organic (posts, comments, subreddits) and promoted (ads, shopping products, their landing pages) text and media content by embedding them into a shared space. Contextual and Behavioral Relevance - Working with Product & Data Science, establishing definitions of what ads are relevant to users and the content we show them next to, building metrics and fine-tuning embeddings to better reflect relevance. Knowledge Graph Embeddings - Building representations for the Knowledge graph entities, e.g., intellectual properties/brands, to be used for high-precision targeting & business insights. User Intent Modeling - Leveraging various techniques to introduce user representations based on the content they interact with: batch & real-time sequence modeling, LLM summarization, etc. LLM-based Representations - Leveraging LLMs, VLMs, and foundational models to build complex representations of Reddit entities that improve ranking outcomes The signals and features we create become a key piece in the Ads Delivery funnel, from targeting to the auction, as well as the Business Insights product and other advertiser-facing products such as Creative generation and optimization. As a Staff ML Engineer , you’ll be in charge of setting the technical direction of multiple pillars the team owns. You will lead cross-functional ML projects end to end - from high-level business gap analysis to engineering execution. Roughly 50% of your time will be spent on technical leadership and mentorship (driving strategy & designs, cross-functional collaboration, raising the quality bar), another 50% being individual hands-on work (data analysis & engineering, modeling & automation). Working closely with team/org leadership developing technical strategy for content-based embeddings & relevance for Ads. Developing new or iterating on existing embedding models for advertising use cases, ranging from aggregation pipelines to two-tower architectures and sequence models. Working with local and 3rd-party LLMs/VLMs: extract representations, develop evaluation methodologies, prompt tune and fine-tune large models to build state-of-the-art embeddings. Building data processing and inference pipelines for the models we develop. Qualitative and quantitative evaluation of the various features we develop, end-to-end experimentation from internal benchmarks to downstream recommender system offline metrics to online experiments. Ensuring the reliability, scalability, and performance of the ML systems by writing automated tests, monitoring performance, and implementing best practices for model management. Participating in modeling and coding reviews: You will review work by other team members and provide feedback to ensure that it meets the team's standards for quality and performance. jobs.title: Threat Detection and Response Engineering Manager
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s mission depends on developing and deploying powerful AI responsibly. Security makes that possible by protecting our research, people, products, and users while enabling progress. We defend sensitive research and other intellectual property, customer data, and the infrastructure behind frontier AI—from GPU supercomputing and multicloud environments to datacenters and emerging agent systems. Threat Detection Engineering builds and operates the detections and investigative workflows that turn adversary activity into effective response. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to guide the engineers who identify and investigate threats to OpenAI and build the capabilities to contain them. You’ll hire and develop engineers, set technical direction, and prioritize risks to OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and critical infrastructure. Your team will take an agent-first approach across the detection and response lifecycle, using OpenAI’s models to develop detections, triage signals, investigate suspicious activity, and support bounded response and continuous improvement. You’ll turn advances in model capability into dependable defenses, own their effectiveness, and work with security, research, and infrastructure partners to ensure findings lead to effective action. You’ll establish where agents can act independently and where human judgment and approval are essential. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Hire, coach, and develop engineers. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, grow technical leadership, and build a team that reviews work rigorously and learns from missed detections and noisy signals. - Set a threat-informed roadmap. Prioritize detection work based on how external and internal actors could target the systems where we train and evaluate frontier models, the production services that run inference and power our products worldwide, the datacenter hardware and networks that support both, and the devices, identities, and applications employees rely on. Balance investment in emerging threats with closing known coverage gaps and keeping existing detections effective. - Own detection and investigation as a complete workflow. Work with infrastructure and system owners to develop and test the controls responders need to contain threats in their environments. Define when human approval is required and how to verify that containment worked. - Apply models across the detection engineering lifecycle. Use OpenAI’s models to help develop threat hypotheses, author and test detections, deploy and tune them, and incorporate investigation findings into better coverage. Drive improvements where missing evidence, unreliable data, or limited controls prevent the team from identifying threats or taking effective action. - Engineer for measurable security outcomes. Use replay, adversarial validation, and regression testing to assess whether workflows find intended threats, distinguish benign activity, and reach defensible conclusions. Establish code review, documentation, staged rollout, monitoring, and rollback practices. Measure coverage, investigation accuracy, time to identify threats, and effectiveness of response. - Contribute during incidents. The Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) leads formal incident response. Your team contributes investigative expertise and uses incident findings to improve detections. You question whether apparent coverage would survive a determined attacker, distinguish plausible explanations from supported conclusions, and stay accountable for threats that existing tools and playbooks miss. - Have managed security or software engineers and can demonstrate how you have hired, coached, developed technical judgment, and improved a team’s ability to deliver. - Are a hands-on builder who can prototype tools, write and review code, and guide engineers through complex detection, investigation, and response designs. - Bring strong AI fluency and have built systems that test how models or agents can improve cyber defense. I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Associate Research Fellow
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY: The key strategic focus within the Internal Medicine Research Unit (IMRU) is identifying novel therapies to prevent or treat metabolic diseases such as obesity and cardiovascular disease. Our goal is to build a world-class research team of dedicated scientists committed to developing a deep mechanistic understanding of the metabolic pathways underlying disease pathogenesis. As a senior scientific leader and member of the obesity discovery biology team, this individual will play a significant role in shaping the scientific direction for the obesity therapeutic area and influencing broader IMRU research strategy and portfolio priorities. The individual will help create and drive discovery research strategy across multiple programs, including target ideation, validation, translational biomarker strategy, hypothesis testing, and early clinical development within the IMRU obesity portfolio. The successful candidate will lead through both direct team leadership and influence across multidisciplinary partners, helping align scientific decisions across discovery biology, translational sciences, clinical, computational, and external collaborators. The individual will identify emerging therapeutic opportunities, advance portfolio programs with scientific rigor and urgency, and represent research strategies to internal leadership and the external scientific community. Knowledge and experience in the study of metabolic pathways are essential, and familiarity with the pathophysiology of dysmetabolic states would be advantageous. Strong self-motivation, excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and the ability to lead, mentor, and build scientific capability in a highly collaborative environment are essential. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES: Shape and influence the scientific direction for discovery research programs aligned with IMRU therapeutic area and portfolio strategy. Apply creative thinking and scientific expertise to formulate strategies that identify, prioritize, and validate therapeutic targets in key areas of interest to the Internal Medicine Research Unit. Maintain awareness of cutting-edge scientific and technical developments in preclinical-to-clinical translation and apply these insights to advance portfolio programs and identify emerging opportunities. Guide research priorities across multiple programs by integrating mechanistic biology, translational feasibility, biomarker strategy, and portfolio impact. Conceptualize, design, and oversee rigorous in vivo, ex vivo, and in vitro studies, including experimental design, data collection, interpretation, and presentation. Quantify and translate experimental results to advance understanding of how metabolic pathways and complex physiological systems are altered by disease and respond to therapeutic intervention. Lead a research team of lab heads and scientists, providing supervision, coaching, and mentorship to develop skills essential to rigorous scientific research and drug discovery execution. Lead through influence across multidisciplinary teams and key stakeholders, driving scientific alignment and decision-making where accountability extends beyond direct reporting lines. Build and facilitate strategic collaborations with partners in the academic scientific community, the broader Pfizer network, and external experts to strengthen scientific insight and portfolio impact. Establish external scientific leadership through peer-reviewed publications, scientific presentations, conference engagement, and thought leadership in relevant areas of metabolic disease biology. Present and represent research programs, portfolio recommendations, and scientific strategy to Pfizer leadership and governance forums. Ensure that all research and discovery work is conducted with the highest quality and ethical standards and in accordance with relevant regulatory, QC, and compliance guidelines. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: PhD, MD, or MD/PhD with postdoctoral research experience and 8+ years of experience in an industry or academic setting. Successful track record of scientific achievement through high-impact publications, presentations, and recognized contributions to the scientific community. Demonstrated ability to critically review complex data, think creatively, formulate novel hypotheses, and translate scientific insight into actionable discovery strategy. Deep expertise in metabolism and/or signaling pathways relevant to obesity (CNS neurocircuitry or peripheral metabolism), with the ability to apply mechanistic insight to therapeutic target identification and validation. Experience performing and/or leading in vitro, in vivo, and ex vivo experiments relevant to metabolic disease biology. Demonstrated ability to influence multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders, including the ability to drive decisions and align priorities without direct authority. Demonstrated ability to contribute to and advance multiple projects in parallel with learning agility, scientific rigor, and portfolio-level judgment. Experience developing scientific talent through mentorship, coaching, and building organizational capability. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to represent research strategy and portfolio recommendations to scientific, governance, and leadership audiences. Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact. NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS: Some travel to scientific conferences and other Pfizer sites expected. ADDITIONAL DETAILS: Last date to apply is November 18, 2026 Work Location Assignment: This is a hybrid role requiring you to live within commuting distance and work on-site an average of 2.5 days per week. The annual base salary for this position ranges from $162,900.00 to $271,500.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. jobs.title: Product Manager, AI
jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: As a Product Manager on Glean's AI team, you will own the core systems that make our AI reliable, efficient, and measurably better over time. We're looking for deep skills and hands-on experience in one or both of the following areas: Agent harness : experience designing or shipping the execution layer around the model, including planning, tool calling, context management, sub-agents, skills, memory, and long-running tasks, and making the tradeoffs across intelligence, latency, and cost that determine how well agents perform. Evaluation : experience building the evalsets, benchmarks, judges, and labeled data that gate launches, compare models and harness changes, and drive continuous hill-climbing on quality. This is a highly technical, cross-functional IC role. You will work closely with AI engineering, data science, and platform marketing teams, and you will partner with leading model providers and help go-to-market teams turn quality improvements into customer proof points. You will: Set the product strategy and roadmap for your area, grounded in customer workflows, trace data, and eval results. Define what "good" looks like for agentic work, including correctness, helpfulness, formatting, efficiency, and reliability, and turn it into clear, measurable launch bars. Make evidence-based tradeoffs across models, prompts, tools, and harness changes, balancing quality against latency, cost, and capacity. Decide when to use frontier models versus post-training open-weight models for specific tasks, weighing quality, cost, latency, and control, and define the data and evals needed to make post-trained models competitive. Build and scale the operating model for evaluation, including datasets, LLM-as-judge systems, human labeling, and benchmarks. Turn failed runs, poor traces, and user feedback into prioritized product and quality improvements. Partner with model providers and strategic partners on model evaluation, launches, and joint quality work. Give the team context, set direction, and build alignment across engineering, data science, and GTM teams without direct authority. About you: You have 4+ years of product management experience, ideally on AI/ML, developer-platform, infrastructure, or quality-tooling products serving large enterprises. You have built or worked closely on LLM-powered agents or at-scale AI products, and you understand how harness design choices affect agent behavior. You are fluent in LLM evaluation concepts: evalsets, LLM-as-judge, pairwise/side-by-side judging, judge calibration against human labels, benchmarks, and offline-versus-online alignment. You are comfortable going deep on agentic systems, including multi-turn tasks, tool use, context and memory management, write actions, and tracing and observability. You are rigorous with data and can turn ambiguous quality problems into crisp hypotheses, metrics, and experiments. You have a strong technical background and can engage credibly with engineers and data scientists on system design and experiment results. You are an excellent written and verbal communicator who enjoys engaging with GTM teams and customers, and you can bridge our technical choices with the outcomes our customers care about. You have a proven track record of taking ownership, taking initiative, and delivering results. You have a learning and growth mindset, and you are mission-first. You are an early adopter of AI in your own product craft, and you use coding agents and AI tools to prototype, analyze, and move faster. Location: This role is hybrid (4 days a week in one of our SF Bay Area offices) Compensation & Benefits: The standard base salary range for this position is $200,000 - $300,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race.

By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. ROLE OVERVIEW Harvey is redefining what’s possible in legal work by combining cutting-edge AI with intuitive product experiences. Agents at Harvey let lawyers turn their expertise into reusable, automated work: custom agents and workflows that draft, review and analyze across a firm’s documents. The Agents team owns Agent Builder, the Agents experience, workflows and the foundations underneath them: orchestration, durable execution, permissions and reliability. Other Harvey products build on this platform as well. As Engineering Manager, you’ll lead a large, senior team of full-stack and backend engineers through the shift from single-turn assistants to long-running, multi-agent systems that firms trust with their most sensitive work. This role is equal parts product judgment and systems depth. We move with urgency, bias toward simplicity, and expect our leaders to be hands-on when needed. cold_email.subject: Interest in Admin Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Admin Coordinator opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Dear Natera Hiring Team,

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. As a contributing member of the Medical Data and Analytics (MD&A) team, you will work closely with cross-functional partners, help ensure analytical quality, and support informed decisions that contribute to improving patient outcomes. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Healthcare, or a related field and 2-4 years of Medical Data Analytics, Commercial Data Analytics, Market Research, Performance Reporting, or related experience. Preferred Qualifications: Apply experience in biotech or pharmaceutical analytics to HCP- or patient-level analyses and subnational market assessments, with attention to data context and business relevance. Perform data extraction, cleaning, and analysis using SQL and Python, and apply familiarity with AI/ML techniques where they can address business needs. Develop or enhance analytical models by preparing inputs, evaluating assumptions, and conducting scenario analyses aligned with strategic objectives; document methods and limitations. Develop and refine dashboards and visualizations in tools such as Databricks, Tableau, or Power BI, and communicate trends and performance metrics in a way that supports stakeholder decisions. Identify and assess analytics opportunities related to service optimization, including automation, capacity assessment, and digital workflow improvements. Coordinate assigned project work by setting milestones, managing dependencies, supporting Agile ceremonies, monitoring KPIs, and communicating progress or risks to relevant partners. Soft Skills: · Communicate clearly in written and verbal formats, tailoring analytical messages to technical and non-technical audiences and contributing effectively to stakeholder discussions. · Manage multiple assignments and shifting priorities independently, maintaining quality and communicating trade-offs or timing risks early. · Demonstrate a collaborative, team-oriented mindset and build productive relationships across functions to achieve shared goals. · Present analytical findings confidently in working sessions and stakeholder forums, responding to questions with clear rationale and appropriate context. · Show initiative in identifying business or data challenges, proposing practical analytical solutions, and following through on agreed actions. · Adapt to changing priorities in a fast-paced environment while maintaining sound judgment, attention to detail, and a focus on patient and business needs. .

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations & Program Excellence Sr Associate — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations & Program Excellence Sr Associate opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin
